rule_name: Check Sheet-Metal Hole-Position Tolerance Against Process Capability
guideline_ref: ISO 2768
description: Checker compares specified hole-position tolerances on sheet-metal parts against typical achievable fabrication capability (process-dependent, e.g. laser vs. punch) and flags tolerances tighter than capability without justification.

rule_name: Flag Flatness/Warpage Risk on Large Thin Molded Surfaces
description: Checker identifies large, thin, or unsupported molded surfaces and compares implied/specified flatness requirements against typical achievable flatness for the feature size, flagging warpage risk.

rule_name: Assign a Defined ISO 286 Fit Class to Mating Hole/Shaft Pairs
guideline_ref: ISO 286
description: Checker verifies every mating hole/shaft interface is assigned an explicit ISO 286 fit designation (clearance, transition, or interference) consistent with the joint's functional requirement (sliding, location, or press-fit).

rule_name: Match IT Grade to Functional Precision Need
guideline_ref: ISO 286
description: Checker verifies the IT (International Tolerance) grade assigned to a toleranced feature is no tighter than needed for its functional precision, avoiding IT grades that exceed process capability or cost targets without justification.

predicate.original_csv_text: example values at 18-30 mm nominal size: IT6 approx 10 micrometers, IT7 approx 16, IT8 approx 25, IT9 approx 40, IT10 approx 64

rule_name: Apply True-Position Tolerancing to Functional/Mating Holes
guideline_ref: ISO 1101
description: Checker verifies functional or mating holes (fastener clearance holes, locating-pin holes) carry a true-position geometric callout referenced to appropriate datums, rather than relying on a plus/minus coordinate tolerance alone.

rule_name: Apply Form/Orientation Controls to Critical Mating or Sealing Surfaces
guideline_ref: ISO 1101
description: Checker verifies flatness, perpendicularity, or parallelism controls are applied to surfaces critical to mating or sealing performance, rather than relying on size tolerance alone to control their form.

rule_name: Avoid Redundant/Conflicting Size-Plus-Geometric Tolerance Callouts
guideline_ref: ISO 8015
description: Checker flags features simultaneously governed by both a plus/minus size dimension and a geometric control covering the same variation, which can create conflicting or ambiguous requirements under the fundamental tolerancing principle.

rule_name: Select Datums Based on Functional Assembly Interfaces
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
description: Reviewer verifies primary, secondary, and tertiary datums are chosen from surfaces/features that are functionally significant to the part's assembly and use (mounting face, locating hole/pin, alignment edge) and reflect the real assembly sequence, not chosen merely for measurement convenience.

rule_name: Verify Datum Reference Frame Fully Constrains Six Degrees of Freedom
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
description: Checker verifies the combination of primary, secondary, and tertiary datums constrains all six degrees of freedom (3 translational, 3 rotational) without redundant or conflicting constraint, per the standard primary=3/secondary=2/tertiary=1 DOF allocation.

rule_name: Maintain Consistent Datum Structure Across Design, Manufacturing, and Inspection
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
description: Reviewer verifies the same datum features and datum reference frame defined on the model/drawing are used for manufacturing fixturing and for inspection/CMM programming, to avoid pass-inspection-but-fails-assembly discrepancies.

rule_name: Identify Critical Dimensional Chains Between Functional Surfaces
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
description: Checker traces chains of toleranced dimensions/features connecting two functionally critical surfaces (e.g. across an assembly gap, mating interface, or clearance path) and flags chains with many links or large cumulative tolerance for dedicated stack-up analysis.

rule_name: Select and Document Worst-Case vs. Statistical (RSS) Stack-Up Method
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
description: Reviewer verifies that, for each identified critical tolerance stack, the appropriate analysis method has been selected and documented — worst-case for safety/interference-critical stacks, statistical/RSS for high-volume manufacturing where some variation cancellation is acceptable.

rule_name: Concentrate Tight Tolerances on Function-Critical Features
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
description: Reviewer verifies tighter tolerances are applied only to dimensions/features that directly affect assembly fit or product function, while non-critical dimensions are left at the relaxed general-tolerance class, per functional dimensioning best practice.

rule_name: Enclosure openings must reject the IP2X jointed test finger (Probe B)
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60529 (IP code) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: No opening path in the enclosure geometry should admit the IEC 61032 Probe B jointed-finger envelope (12mm dia segment, 80mm knurled length, two pivot joints bending up to 90 deg, 50mm x 20mm baffle stop) to reach live/hazardous internal parts.

rule_name: IP1X-level openings must reject 50mm back-of-hand test sphere
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: No opening should allow a 50mm-diameter rigid sphere (back-of-hand surrogate) to pass through to a hazard, for the lowest IP first-digit protection tier.

rule_name: IP3X-level openings must reject 2.5mm tool/wire probe
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: No opening should allow a 2.5mm-diameter rigid probe (representing tools/wires) to reach hazardous internal parts, for IP first-digit level 3 enclosures.

rule_name: IP4X-level openings must reject 1.0mm fine wire probe
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: No opening should allow a 1.0mm-diameter rigid wire probe to reach hazardous internal parts, for IP first-digit level 4 enclosures (finest openings before dust-protection tiers).

rule_name: Straight rigid test pin check for slots with unobstructed line-of-sight to hazard
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: For slot/vent geometries with a straight, unobstructed line-of-sight path to a live or hazardous part, verify the minimum cross-section rejects the applicable rigid test probe diameter (no articulation needed for a straight-through path).

rule_name: Enclosure seams/vents must not present a direct path for vertically falling drops (IPX1)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify that any top-facing opening, seam, or vent does not create a straight vertical path from outside to internal electrical parts, for the lowest IP second-digit (dripproof) tier.

rule_name: Enclosure geometry must tolerate 15-degree tilted drop ingress (IPX2)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify sealed seams/openings remain protected when the product is modeled tilted up to 15 degrees from its normal drip-test orientation, per the IP second-digit level 2 tier.

rule_name: Vents/seams must reject 60-degree angled spray (IPX3) without direct path to live parts
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify that any external opening does not present a direct unobstructed path to hazardous internal parts when water is modeled arriving at up to 60 degrees from vertical, for IPX3-rated zones.

rule_name: Splash-protected geometry must block ingress from any direction (IPX4)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify enclosure seams and openings have no direct line-of-sight path to hazardous internal parts from any azimuth/elevation angle, for IPX4-rated splashproof zones (e.g. wet-area vacuum/appliance housings).

rule_name: Jet-resistant seals must withstand a 6.3mm nozzle jet without ingress path (IPX5)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify that seam/vent gap geometry does not admit a modeled 6.3mm-diameter directed water jet to hazardous internal parts, for IPX5-rated zones.

rule_name: Immersion-rated housings must locate all seams/vents above or sealed below the specified test depth (IPX7)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
description: Verify that for IPX7-rated products, any non-fully-sealed seam, button boot, or vent is either watertight or positioned/rated for the 1m/30min immersion envelope.

rule_name: Small square/rectangular openings require minimum hazard-zone setback distance
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
description: For a square opening with side length between roughly 12mm and 20mm, verify the internal hazard (e.g. rotating brush roll, blade) is set back at least the published minimum distance from the opening plane.

predicate.original_csv_text: Opening side 12-20 mm requires hazard zone >=120 mm away (worked example, public summary of ISO 13857 Table 4/5)

rule_name: Safety distances must account for both adult (14+) and child (3+) reach-through geometry
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
description: Verify hazard setback distances are checked against two separate anthropometric population cases where a product may be accessible to children: the general (14 years and older, 95th percentile) case and the supplementary child (3 years and older) case for reaching through openings.

rule_name: Reach-over protective structure height/depth combination must exceed hazard access envelope
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
description: For guards or housings that a user could reach over (e.g. top of a tall appliance) rather than through an opening, verify the combination of barrier height and horizontal distance to the hazard exceeds the reach-over envelope defined by ISO 13857.

rule_name: Reach-under gaps beneath the product must impede lower-limb access to hazards
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
description: Verify that any gap beneath a floor-standing or countertop appliance through which a foot or leg could reach is either too small or positioned far enough from moving/hot/live parts, per ISO 13857 lower-limb guidance.

rule_name: Minimum creepage path length along insulation surfaces between live conductors
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
description: Verify the shortest path measured along the surface of solid insulation between two conductors at different potentials meets or exceeds the minimum required for the working voltage, pollution degree, and material CTI group; ribs/grooves may be needed to lengthen the surface path within the same footprint.

rule_name: Minimum through-air clearance between conductors at different potentials
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
description: Verify the shortest straight-line (through-air) distance between two conductors at different potentials meets or exceeds the minimum required for the working voltage and overvoltage category.

rule_name: Insulation surface routing (ribs/grooves) used to increase effective creepage path without increasing footprint
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
description: Where direct creepage distance is insufficient within the available footprint, verify that ribs, grooves, or barrier walls are modeled to increase the effective along-surface path length between conductors.

rule_name: Guard/vent openings near moving parts must combine probe-rejection and setback-distance rules
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / ISO 13857 (safety distances) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: For any guard, grille, or vent adjacent to a moving hazard (e.g. brush roll, fan, gears), verify the opening simultaneously rejects the applicable IEC 61032 test probe AND, where the probe geometry alone is insufficient, provides the ISO 13857 minimum setback distance from the opening to the hazard.

rule_name: Rotating-part guard slot width must remain smaller than the probe/finger geometry it must reject
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: Verify slot widths in guards over rotating parts (e.g. brush-bar covers, fan grilles) are dimensioned below the rejection threshold for the applicable IP first-digit/IEC 61032 probe, independent of the setback-distance rule.

rule_name: Handheld/grip surfaces require material and geometry flag for touch-temperature review
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: Flag any user-touched surface (handle, trigger, grip) that is within a defined proximity of a heat-generating component (motor, battery, heater element) for touch-temperature engineering review; geometry alone cannot certify compliance without material and thermal simulation data.

rule_name: Externally accessible surfaces near heat sources require setback or shielding geometry
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: Verify externally accessible enclosure surfaces near a heat source (e.g. dryer barrel, motor housing) either maintain a minimum standoff distance or include a shielding/venting geometry, pending thermal simulation to confirm surface temperature stays within the applicable touch-temperature class.

rule_name: Full articulated-probe accessibility simulation is flagged as not yet computable
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes)
description: Record that a true geometric simulation of the IEC 61032 jointed test finger's reachable envelope through complex, multi-surface enclosure openings (accounting for all articulation angles and insertion paths) is not implemented in the current automated checker and requires either simplified bounding-geometry proxies or manual physical probe testing.

rule_name: Openings with re-entrant or non-convex geometry require manual probe-path review
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes)
description: Flag any enclosure opening whose internal geometry is non-convex (e.g. has internal pockets, undercuts, or multiple connected cavities) for manual jointed-probe accessibility review, since automated straight-line/bounding-box checks are unreliable for such shapes.

rule_name: Large plastic components should reserve a marking area for generic material identification
guideline_ref: ISO 11469 / ISO 1043 (plastics marking)
description: Where product-specific marking requirements apply, verify major plastic parts include a legible, accessible surface area (boss, flat, or recess) for a molded-in or applied material identification mark; ISO 11469 leaves exact size/location to manufacturer agreement rather than prescribing a universal dimension.

rule_name: Material identification symbol must use standard ISO 1043 abbreviations where marking is applied
guideline_ref: ISO 11469 / ISO 1043 (plastics marking)
description: Where a part is marked per ISO 11469, verify the symbol used is a valid abbreviated term/symbol from the ISO 1043 series (basic polymers, fillers, plasticizers, flame retardants) rather than a free-text or proprietary code.

rule_name: Fasteners and joints intended for end-of-life disassembly must remain tool-accessible
guideline_ref: IEC 62430 (ecodesign)
description: Verify that fasteners/joints identified as disassembly points (for material separation or repair) have unobstructed tool access geometry (clearance for driver/tool head and swing arc) rather than being trapped behind non-removable co-molded or bonded features.

rule_name: Product design must undergo an environmentally-conscious design (ECD) checkpoint gate before geometry freeze
guideline_ref: IEC 62430 (ecodesign)
description: Record whether the design has passed a documented environmental-aspect review (materials, disassembly, recyclability, lifecycle impacts) consistent with the IEC 62430 process stages, as a qualitative gate rather than a geometric measurement.

rule_name: Energy-source safeguard separation must reflect IEC 62368-1 hazard-based classification
description: For products with ICT/AV-adjacent subsystems (e.g. connected appliance electronics), verify that physical separation/safeguard geometry between a classified energy source (electrical, mechanical, thermal) and an ordinary person corresponds to the hazard-based safeguard approach, rather than assuming a single fixed clearance for all energy types.

rule_name: Household appliance enclosures must prevent probe access to both live parts and moving parts
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
description: Verify enclosure/guard openings are checked against test-probe accessibility rules for two separate hazard classes identified in IEC 60335-1: live electrical parts and moving mechanical parts, since acceptance criteria/probe types can differ between the two.
